name: Page Anatomy
description: How FlowX platform pages are put together: four page levels signalled by the navigation frame, a shared title-card + main-card spine, three resource-list render modes, the regular resource page layout, and four main-card variants. This is a structural/composition pattern; assemble new pages from these named parts instead of inventing a layout. The wireframes on the page are illustrative skeletons, not pixel specs; for exact surfaces use cards.json, values-table.json, tabs.json, and empty-states.json.

pageBackground.note: grey app background the cards sit on (see patterns/cards.json)

shared.spine: Nearly every page is a title card that names the resource, followed by the content below it (usually a single main card). Deliberate exceptions like canvas editors are the only pages without this spine.

levels.note: Every screen sits at one of four levels, and the navigation frame signals which one. The higher the level, the more navigation is present; drilling into a resource replaces the nav with a back breadcrumb.

workspaceOrg.label: Workspace / Org level
workspaceOrg.navFrame: No top command bar. A left sidebar carries the brand, the workspace or organization switcher, the labelled nav, and the user profile pinned at the bottom.
workspaceOrg.content: A system alert banner may sit above the content, then the page body.

project.label: Project level
project.navFrame: The top command bar appears together with the full labelled left nav.
project.content: A page title card and the resource list.

insideResourceCanvas.label: Inside a resource, canvas
insideResourceCanvas.navFrame: A subheader with a back breadcrumb appears; the nav collapses to an icon rail.
insideResourceCanvas.content: A full-width canvas with side panels.

insideResourceRegular.label: Inside a resource, regular page
insideResourceRegular.navFrame: A subheader with a back breadcrumb; the breadcrumb can run two to four levels deep and is the way back out. The nav is hidden.
insideResourceRegular.content: The regular resource page body: title card plus main card.

renderModes.note: A resource list can be laid out three ways, whatever it contains. The layout is a treatment, not a new page: the title card and the spine stay the same.

tables.label: Tables
tables.description: One or more tables inside the main card, each under its own sub-header.
tables.whenToUse: The default layout for entity lists.

nestedCards.label: Nested cards
nestedCards.description: A grid of secondary cards inside the main card, one per entity, each with its own inline actions.

primaryCards.label: Primary cards
primaryCards.description: No main card. Each entity is its own primary card, stacked directly under the title card.

regularResourcePage.note: The regular resource page has one spine: a title card that names the resource, followed by the content below it.

mainOption.label: Title card + Main card
mainOption.description: One title card, one main card holding all the content.
mainOption.whenToUse: The default for records and settings.

cardGridVariant.label: Title card + multiple small cards
cardGridVariant.description: The main card is replaced by a grid of small cards, one per entity or capability, each with its own inline actions. Used when the content is a set of independent peers.

mainCardVariants.note: The main card comes in four variants, chosen by how much the resource carries. When a record has more than a couple of fields, its one or two defining fields stay in the top card, which becomes a config card, and everything else moves into tabs.

withoutTabs.label: Without tabs
withoutTabs.description: A single group of fields with footer actions (Reset / Save bottom-right).
withoutTabs.whenToUse: Simple one-facet resources, such as a connection form.

withTabs.label: With tabs
withTabs.description: The top card becomes a config card that keeps the record's one or two defining fields; a tab bar in the main card splits the rest into facets, each tab holding its own content (such as a table with its own Add action).

withTabsAndColumns.label: With tabs and columns
withTabsAndColumns.description: Inside a tab, peer sections sit in two columns when they have no natural order. A section header can carry an enable toggle that gates the whole section, and a section toggled off collapses to its header.

withSplitPane.label: With a split pane
withSplitPane.description: For operation editors the tab content splits in two: inputs on the left, live output on the right (such as a code preview, a results console, or a query builder).

groundRules.title: Title card, then main card
groundRules.rule: The spine of nearly every page. The few exceptions, like canvas editors, are deliberate.

groundRules.title: Identity first, details in tabs
groundRules.rule: The one or two defining fields sit in the top config card. Everything else goes into a tab.

groundRules.title: Commit in the footer, act in the section
groundRules.rule: Reset and Save sit bottom-right of the main card. Local actions like Add or Test sit next to what they change. Nothing floats in between.

groundRules.title: Stack when order matters, columns when it doesn't
groundRules.rule: Sections that depend on each other read top to bottom. Peers with no natural sequence can share a row.

groundRules.title: Show state before detail
groundRules.rule: Enable toggles gate sections, status pills mark rows. State is visible before anything is opened.

groundRules.title: No page renders blank
groundRules.rule: Every list ships an empty state and every result pane says what to do first (see patterns/empty-states.json).

themes.dark: not documented; the pattern page keeps its wireframes light
